title: Insulation Rebates in Kamloops 2026: Up to $5,500 from BC Hydro
desc: Half of Kamloops households live in homes built before 1981, and January lows average -6.1°C. BC Hydro's insulation formula and Kamloops installers ranked by Google reviews.
lead: Kamloops is dry, cold and old. Half its households live in homes built before 1981, and winter lows can drop below -30°C. That is where insulation does the most work.
cards_heading: What BC Hydro pays for insulation in Kamloops
cards_intro: We re-read BC Hydro's insulation page on October 2, 2026. The rebate is for homes heated mainly by electricity. FortisBC lists the same formula for its gas customers.

cards.title: Attic
cards.amount: $0.02 x R added x sq ft
cards.note: Capped at $900, at least R12 added.

cards.title: Walls and basement
cards.amount: $0.09 x R added x sq ft
cards.note: Capped at $1,200 each for wall cavity, sheathing, and basement or crawlspace.

cards.title: Floors and other spots
cards.amount: $0.07 x R added x sq ft
cards.note: Capped at $1,000, at least R20 added.

cards.title: More than one upgrade
cards.note: For finishing more than one eligible upgrade.

after_cards:
A Kamloops bungalow

A 1,100 square foot attic at R-12 brought to R-50 adds R-38. The formula gives 0.02 x 38 x 1,100 = $836. Add R-12 to 1,000 square feet of wall cavity for 0.09 x 12 x 1,000 = $1,080. The total is $1,916 by our reading of the published formula.
sections:
The 2021 Census counted 39,915 households in Kamloops. Of those, 20,275 (51%) live in homes built before 1981, and 9,895 are owner-occupied detached houses from that time. Detached houses make up 50% of all households. Only 19% live in apartments.

About 5.1% of households told the census their home needs major repairs. If yours has a wet attic or old vermiculite, deal with that before insulating.

Kamloops's average January low from 2015 to 2024 was -6.1°C and the coldest day in that record reached -34.3°C. Summers are hot and dry, so insulation works against heat gain too. A well-insulated attic can cut cooling loads as well.
If the old insulation is removed

When old material is pulled out because of pests or moisture, BC Hydro assumes a starting R-value based on the age of the home and pays on the difference. In an older house that can mean a bigger rebate on a full re-do. Put both R-values on the invoice.

BC Hydro accepts batts, loose fill, board and spray foam. A Kamloops bungalow with an open attic usually gets loose fill to add depth. Rigid board and spray foam suit basement walls and rim joists. Compare quotes by finished R-value, not by thickness. The rebate cannot be more than the invoice shows you paid.

Hot dry summers make the attic as important as the walls. A dark roof can push attic air well above outdoor temperatures, so a thicker layer slows that heat from reaching the rooms below.

BC Hydro sends income-qualified customers to the CleanBC Better Homes Energy Savings Program instead, and the two cannot be combined. The 2026 program document has no insulation or window rebates. The free Energy Conservation Assistance Program may include insulation, so ask there before you pay for any work.

• The home must be mainly electric-heated and at least 12 months old.
  • An HPCN member must do the work.
  • Work required for a permitted addition does not qualify.
  • Apply within six months of the invoice date.
claim_steps: Confirm the home is electric-heated and the account is in your name.
Ask for a quote that lists the existing R-value, the added R-value and the area.
Add another eligible upgrade to check the bonus.
